applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision over Matthew 1:20 by citing the challenger's and defender's chain readings, so K-C governs the weighing.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase UNDERDETERMINED with the reason that the challenger answered one way and the defender another: one reading is that the judge weighed the two chains by footing and found neither decisive; the other is that the judge merely noted conflicting chain answers and did not weigh by footing. I adopt the latter because no footing comparison is written.
why: The judge declared the point underdetermined because each side supplied a chain answer, without weighing the two chains by footing as K-C requires.
